node.label: J. R. McNeill
node.description: An environmental historian who works at global and regional scales. Something New Under the Sun (2000) is an environmental history of the twentieth-century world. Mosquito Empires (2010) argues that ecological change made the Greater Caribbean hospitable to the mosquitoes that carry yellow fever and malaria. Because survivors gained immunity or resistance, these diseases took sides in the struggles for empire and revolution between 1620 and 1914, decimating forces sent from Europe. His survey of the field credits the Annales with an inspiring general approach while noting how little environmental history its founders wrote, and treats Alfred Crosby’s studies of ecological exchange as landmarks. In his 2020 AHA presidential address he argues that scientific evidence can illuminate histories poorly documented in writing, while warning against monocausal climate histories and against letting a new tool dictate the question.
